name: Loki + MinIO
tagline: Logs indexed by labels, chunks in S3 storage, traces beside them in Tempo.

howItWorks.title: Write path
howItWorks.body:
Alloy pushes batches to the distributor over HTTP or OTLP.
The distributor validates, rate-limits and hashes each stream onto the ring.
Ingesters append to a chunk in memory and write a WAL.
Full or idle chunks flush to MinIO as objects.

howItWorks.title: Index and chunks
howItWorks.body:
Chunks are compressed log lines for one stream.
The TSDB index maps label sets and time to chunks.
Index files upload to the same bucket via the shipper.
A schema_config entry pins index type and schema from a date.

howItWorks.title: Labels and cardinality
howItWorks.body:
One unique label set is one stream with its own chunks.
Keep labels few and stable: namespace, app, env, level.
Never label by user ID, request ID or IP.
Put variable data in the line or structured metadata.

howItWorks.title: LogQL
howItWorks.body:
A stream selector uses the index: {app="checkout", env="prod"}.
Line filters come next, then parsers: | json, | logfmt.
Label filters refine: | status >= 500.
Metric queries turn logs into numbers: rate(...[5m]).

howItWorks.title: Traces, storage and retention
howItWorks.body:
Alloy sends traces to Tempo; trace_id links a log line to its trace.
Loki uses the s3 backend with s3forcepathstyle against MinIO.
The compactor deletes data older than retention_period.
Per-stream retention overrides apply through retention_stream rules.

flow: The application emits structured logs and spans over OTLP.
Alloy receives OTLP and batches it.
Logs go to Loki, traces go to Tempo.
The distributor hashes each stream onto the ingester ring.
Ingesters fill chunks in memory and write the WAL.
Flushed chunks and index files land in MinIO.
A LogQL query is split by time and sent to queriers.
Queriers read the index, then fetch chunks from MinIO and ingesters.

deploy.summary: Single-binary Loki 3.1, Tempo, Alloy and MinIO under Docker Compose on one Linux VM.
prerequisites: Linux VM with Docker Engine 24+ and Compose v2
Static IP and DNS name for the VM
About 4 GB RAM and a dedicated data disk

steps.title: Prepare the host
steps.code:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/obs && cd /opt/obs
printf 'MINIO_ROOT_USER=minioadmin\nMINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=CHANGE-ME-32-chars\n' | sudo tee .env >/dev/null
sudo chmod 600 .env
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 3100,4317,4318 proto tcp   # placeholder subnet
steps.note: Replace the password and subnet. Only the trusted subnet reaches Loki and OTLP.

steps.title: Compose file
steps.code:
services:
  minio:
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-06-13T22-53-53Z
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:?set in .env}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set in .env}
    volumes: [minio-data:/data]
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:9000:9000", "127.0.0.1:9001:9001"]
  minio-init:
    image: minio/mc:RELEASE.2024-06-12T14-34-03Z
    depends_on: [minio]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "until mc alias set local http://minio:9000 $${MINIO_ROOT_USER} $${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}; do sleep 2; done &&
      mc mb --ignore-existing local/loki-data"
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.1.0
    command: ["-config.file=/etc/loki/loki.yaml", "-config.expand-env=true"]
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    volumes: ["./loki.yaml:/etc/loki/loki.yaml:ro", "loki-data:/loki"]
    depends_on:
      minio-init: {condition: service_completed_successfully}
    ports: ["3100:3100"]
  tempo:
    image: grafana/tempo:2.5.0
    command: ["-config.file=/etc/tempo.yaml"]
    volumes: ["./tempo.yaml:/etc/tempo.yaml:ro", "tempo-data:/var/tempo"]
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:3200:3200"]
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.2.0
    command: ["run", "--server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345", "/etc/alloy/config.alloy"]
    volumes: ["./config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro"]
    depends_on: [loki, tempo]
    ports: ["4317:4317", "4318:4318", "127.0.0.1:12345:12345"]
volumes:
  minio-data: {}
  loki-data: {}
  tempo-data: {}
steps.note: Save as /opt/obs/compose.yaml. MinIO binds to localhost; verify the pinned tags exist in your registry.

steps.title: Loki config with MinIO
steps.code:
auth_enabled: false
server:
  http_listen_port: 3100
common:
  path_prefix: /loki
  replication_factor: 1
  ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory
  storage:
    s3:
      endpoint: minio:9000
      bucketnames: loki-data
      access_key_id: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER}
      secret_access_key: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
      s3forcepathstyle: true
      insecure: true
schema_config:
  configs:
    - from: 2024-04-01
      store: tsdb
      object_store: s3
      schema: v13
      index:
        prefix: index_
        period: 24h
storage_config:
  tsdb_shipper:
    active_index_directory: /loki/tsdb-index
    cache_location: /loki/tsdb-cache
compactor:
  working_directory: /loki/compactor
  retention_enabled: true
  delete_request_store: s3
limits_config:
  retention_period: 168h
  allow_structured_metadata: true
  max_label_names_per_series: 15
ingester:
  wal:
    dir: /loki/wal
analytics:
  reporting_enabled: false
steps.note: Save as loki.yaml. insecure true is lab-only; use TLS to MinIO and replication 3 in production.

steps.title: Tempo config
steps.code:
server:
  http_listen_port: 3200
distributor:
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        grpc:
          endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317
storage:
  trace:
    backend: local
    wal:
      path: /var/tempo/wal
    local:
      path: /var/tempo/blocks
steps.note: Save as tempo.yaml. Local block storage for the lab; point it at S3 for production.

steps.title: Alloy pipeline
steps.note: Save as config.alloy. Loki 3 accepts OTLP natively at /otlp; resource attributes become labels or structured metadata.

steps.title: Run under systemd
steps.code:
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/obs.service >/dev/null <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Loki, Tempo, MinIO and Alloy
Requires=docker.service
After=docker.service network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
WorkingDirectory=/opt/obs
ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker compose up -d
ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker compose down

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now obs.service
steps.note: The stack now starts at boot.

steps.title: Push and query a line
steps.code:
NOW=$(date +%s)000000000
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/push -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"streams\":[{\"stream\":{\"app\":\"demo\",\"env\":\"lab\"},\"values\":[[\"$NOW\",\"level=error msg=hello\"]]}]}"
curl -sG http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/query_range --data-urlencode 'query={app="demo"} |= "error"'

steps.title: Find chunks in MinIO
steps.code:
cd /opt/obs && docker compose restart loki
docker compose run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh minio-init -c \
 'mc alias set l http://minio:9000 "$MINIO_ROOT_USER" "$MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD" && mc ls --recursive l/loki-data | head'
steps.note: Restarting Loki forces a flush; otherwise wait for chunk idle time.

pitfalls: High-cardinality labels bloat the index and slow every query.
MinIO needs s3forcepathstyle true; the bucket must exist before Loki starts.
retention_period does nothing without compactor retention_enabled and delete_request_store.
Edit schema_config by adding a future-dated entry, never by changing an old one.
Clock skew makes Loki reject out-of-order or too-old entries.
replication_factor 1 with an inmemory ring loses recent logs on a crash.
Promtail is in maintenance mode; start new work on Alloy.
keyPoints: Loki indexes labels only; log lines stay in compressed chunks.
MinIO holds chunks and index files over the S3 API.
Alloy pushes OTLP logs to Loki and traces to Tempo.
Few stable labels keep cardinality, cost and queries healthy.
quickDeploy: Run MinIO, Loki, Tempo and Alloy with Compose
Point loki.yaml at the MinIO bucket
Send OTLP through Alloy to both backends
Query with LogQL and find chunks in MinIO
osiNote: Speaks HTTP, gRPC and S3 over TCP.
production: Run replication_factor 3 with WAL on persistent disks.
Enable compactor retention; set per-tenant limits and stream rules.
Back up the MinIO bucket; use erasure coding across drives.
Enforce TLS to MinIO and keep credentials in a secrets store.
Alert on ingester flush failures, 429 rate limits and active streams.
